persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Wanjiru, 18, visiting your grandmother, Cucu Njoki Wambui, in Othaya, Nyeri. Cucu is 79 and knows wonderful stories about her life, but nobody has ever written them down. Today you sit beside her with your phone, ask her the questions, and start her life-story book.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called In My Own Words. You have never seen it before, and that is fine.
First, the problem. Every family has great stories. How Grandmother met Grandfather. The house where she grew up. How the family survived the hard years.
But these stories are almost never written down. One day the person who knew them is gone, and the stories are gone too.
In My Own Words fixes that. It asks one gentle question at a time. The person answers, and the app writes the answers into a book, chapter by chapter.
Who uses it? Older people who want to leave their story for their children. And often a grandchild, who sits next to a grandparent, asks the questions, and holds the phone.
The app was made in America, but the questions about birth, school, love, work and faith fit any family, anywhere.
Let us walk through the Home page, from the top.

lines.t: At the top is a card called Today's page. It is a small diary with one question about your day. Today we focus on the life story below it.
Next is a box with the words Whose story is this. Type the name of the person whose life this book is about. That name goes on the cover of the book.
Then comes a card called The people in your story. Type a name in the Name box and choose how the person is related, for example Spouse, which means husband or wife, or Grandchild. Then tap plus Add.
Below that is a card called This week's question. It gives one new question every week.
Then the most important part: Chapters of your life. There are seven chapters, like Beginnings, Growing up, and Love and marriage. Each chapter has four questions.

lines: Tap a chapter, and the question screen opens. At the top it tells you the chapter and the question number, for example question 1 of 4. The question is written in big letters.
Under the question is a big red button with a microphone. In real life, Grandmother presses it and talks, and her words appear in the box below.
But for this test, please type the answers in the box. Do not use the red button. Typing makes sure every name and place is spelled correctly.
Under the box is a line called Who is in this story. The people you added on Home appear there. Tap a name to mark that this person was in this story.
When the answer is ready, tap the green button, Save and next question. Back goes to the question before. All chapters, at the top, takes you back to Home.
Be careful to put each answer under the right question. Read the question first, then type the answer that fits it.

lines.t: Back on Home, there is a card called The Key. It tells the family where important things are kept, for example where the photo albums are. Never write passwords there.

lines: Then the gold button, See your book so far. It shows the cover with the name, then each chapter, each answer, and who was in each story.
Everything stays on this phone. Nothing is sent to anyone.
To start again with an empty book, scroll to the very bottom of the Home page and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. The app asks twice before it erases anything.
In the test, you will be a grandchild helping your grandmother start her book. Take your time. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Wanjiru, sitting with Cucu Njoki. The book is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Please TYPE every answer (do not use the red microphone button). When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open In My Own Words with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If a menu asking 'What would you like to do?' covers the page, tap '↩ Pick up where I left off' first. Then scroll to the very bottom of the Home page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The name box is empty, the people card says 'No one added yet', and every chapter says '4 questions'. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: This book is Cucu's life story. Put her name, Njoki Wambui, on the book.
tasks.hint: Look near the top of the Home page for the box that asks whose story this is.

tasks.text: Add the people in Cucu's story: her husband Kariuki, and you, her granddaughter Wanjiru. Choose the right relation for each.
tasks.hint: Use the card 'The people in your story' on Home. Spouse means husband or wife. You are her grandchild.

tasks.text: Cucu says: "I was born in 1946 in Othaya, in a round house with a grass roof." Type this answer under the question that fits it.
tasks.hint: It is about where she was born. Open the chapter about the start of her life and read each question until you find the one about being born.

tasks.text: Cucu says: "I met Kariuki at a church harambee in Karatina. He was carrying a big basket of bananas." Type this under the question that fits it, and show that Kariuki was in this story.
tasks.hint: It is about the day she met her husband: look in the Love & marriage chapter. Then tap Kariuki's name under 'Who is in this story?'.

tasks.text: Cucu keeps all her old photo albums in a blue tin box under her bed. Write this where the family will find it at the end of the book.
tasks.hint: On the Home page, find the card that tells the family where pictures and important things are kept.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: records a person's life stories, one question at a time
you can talk (or type) and it writes the answers down
it makes a book for the family to keep

daily.task: Add one memory in In My Own Words: answer one question with two or three sentences (a made-up or a happy real memory).
